source.title: LLM Self-Recognition: Steering and Retrieving Activation Signatures
source.authors: Thibaud Ardoin; Jonas Schäfer; G. Wunder

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses subliminal learning as an analogy, but its experiments concern activation-based self-recognition and retrieval of deliberately injected steering signatures, not teacher-to-student transmission of traits.
record.gate_note: The paper cites subliminal learning and compares its reported architecture boundary with cross-model transfer of deliberately injected steering signatures. It does not test trait transmission, filtered teacher outputs, or any of the listed claim versions. The cross-model signature results are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The paper only draws an analogy to subliminal learning. Its experiments steer a model's activations at inference with random sparse vectors, then retrieve these deliberately injected signatures with probes. No student is fine-tuned on teacher outputs and no trait is measured, so no claim version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors' main conclusions are that LLMs self-recognise their outputs via linearly separable activation signals, and that sparse random steering gives a robust, low-cost attribution watermark. The subliminal-learning analogy is a side remark about the cross-architecture boundary and is not tested.
record.recipe_differences: The study injects random sparse vectors into activations at inference time and evaluates signature retrieval; it does not fine-tune students on teacher-generated data.
record.method_sensitivity: Cross-architecture transfer degrades to chance; transfer partially persists between Llama-3.1-8B Base and Instruct versions.

fits_no_version.finding: Random sparse steering signatures can be retrieved by a probe trained on the generating model's activations. Retrieval partially survives a switch between Llama-3.1-8B Base and Instruct, and falls to near chance (text F1 about 0.51–0.65) for texts generated by Ministral-3-8B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-level signatures injected at generation are geometrically coherent within a model family but not across architectures.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The results relevant by analogy concern injected-signature retrieval rather than trait transmission. The flattened Table 9 does not support confident assignment of its individual values to model/dataset cells, and the cross-model results report no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were included: the paper's self-recognition, watermark robustness, and generation-quality experiments do not measure teacher-to-student trait transmission or its predicted behavior.

untested.parts: All: no fine-tuning on teacher-generated filtered data and no trait acquisition.
All: the architecture boundary concerns probe retrieval of injected signatures, not trait transmission between teacher and student.
All: no analysis of what carries a teacher-to-student signal.
All: the steering is applied to activations, and no trait shift caused by prompt tokens is measured.

record.verdict_notes: Table 10 (cross-model self-recognition accuracy) is likewise unrelated to the claim, so omitting it is appropriate.

versions.untested_parts: Teacher-generated, semantically unrelated and filtered training data; acquisition of the teacher's trait.
Whether trait transmission depends on teacher and student sharing a base model.
Transmission of misalignment or other alignment-relevant traits.
The mechanism carrying a teacher-to-student trait signal.
Robustness of trait transmission to full fine-tuning, LoRA ranks, or evaluation prompts different from training.
A prompt-only trait shift from linked tokens without fine-tuning.

rows.subject: Cross-model steering-vector attribution (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated binary classification of texts generated with distinct steering vectors, extracting activations with the training model.

conditions.value: Different generating architecture (Ministral-3-8B-Base); cross-evaluation on the listed datasets.

rows.measure: Token-level and text-level F1 for steering-vector classification
rows.value: Chance level, regardless of dataset (authors' explicit description; Table 9 values cannot be assigned confidently from the flattened layout).
rows.locator: Section 6, Cross-Dataset and Cross-Model Generalization; Table 9
rows.note: This measures retrieval of deliberately injected steering signatures, not transmission of a behavioral trait. The table layout does not support safely assigning its individual flattened values to particular model/dataset cells.
rows.check: The source is Appendix G (Table 9), which Section 6 points to, not Section 6 itself. The Ministral-3-8B-Base column can be read: token/text F1 of 0.55/0.52, 0.56/0.61, 0.58/0.51 and 0.61/0.65, against a binary chance level of 0.5. This is near chance, as the authors say. The row records signature retrieval, not trait transmission.

source_check.correct: Subject: detector/training models Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (trained on ELI5) and Llama-3.1-8B (trained on News); generating model Ministral-3-8B-Base. Baseline: in-distribution (bold diagonal) token/text F1 0.90/0.99 for both training setups; chance for binary is about 0.5. Value as numbers: the Ministral-3-8B-Base column of Table 9 reads 0.55/0.52, 0.56/0.61 (News) and 0.58/0.51, 0.61/0.65 (ELI5), which supports 'chance level'.
source_check.locator_found: The 'chance level, regardless of dataset' sentence is on page 7 near the heading '6. Related Work' (placement garbled by two-column extraction). Table 9 is in Appendix G, 'Cross-Dataset and Cross-Model Generalization'.
source_check.problem: Value matches the authors' words, but the subject says 'not stated' though the text names the models, and the in-distribution baseline 0.90/0.99 is given.

relation.reason: The study goes beyond a citation: it interprets its own cross-architecture boundary as mirroring subliminal learning's same-base requirement (page 7 and Appendix G). It does not test or use the effect.

tranche.reason: The study injects random sparse steering vectors at inference and probes for them. No student is fine-tuned on teacher outputs and no trait transmission is measured. The cross-architecture result is the authors' own analogy to Cloud et al. and does not test version B.

source_check.notes: The rows measure probe retrieval of deliberately injected steering signatures, a different construct from trait transmission, so versions none is right. Table 9 can be rebuilt from the flattened text: train rows are Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct/ELI5 and Llama-3.1-8B/News; test columns are Instruct ELI5/News, Llama-3.1-8B News/ELI5 and Ministral-3-8B-Base News/ELI5.
